resource_load.note: Unbounded N: no pagination on the find query

performance_issues.description: db.Find called without ListOptions (no pagination), loading ALL matching notifications for the repo into memory
performance_issues.impact: If a user has thousands of unread notifications for a repo, all are loaded at once causing memory pressure and slow queries
performance_issues.recommendation: Add ListOptions to opts or use a batch-update query instead of per-item loop

performance_issues.description: For each notification: SetNotificationStatus does SELECT+UPDATE (2 queries), LoadAttributes does 4 SELECTs (repo, issue, user, comment), ToNotificationThread does GetIndividualUserRepoPermission + GetLastComment (2 more). Total: ~8 DB round-trips per notification.
performance_issues.impact: 100 notifications = ~800 DB queries in a single request
performance_issues.recommendation: Use batch UPDATE query, then batch-load attributes using NotificationList.LoadAttributes pattern

optimization_recommendations.description: Replace per-item SetNotificationStatus loop with a single batch UPDATE
optimization_recommendations.estimated_impact: Reduce N*2 queries to 1 query for the status update
optimization_recommendations.implementation: UPDATE notification SET status=? WHERE id IN (?) AND user_id=?

optimization_recommendations.description: Add pagination or a hard limit to the initial find query
optimization_recommendations.estimated_impact: Prevent unbounded memory usage and query time
optimization_recommendations.implementation: Add ListOptions with a reasonable max (e.g., 1000) or paginate

performance_issues.description: GetNotificationByID is called twice: once in getThread and once inside SetNotificationStatus
performance_issues.impact: 1 extra SELECT per request (minor for single-item endpoint)
performance_issues.recommendation: Pass the already-fetched notification to avoid re-fetch, or accept the minor overhead
